procedure: Facet joint injection / medial branch block / radiofrequency ablation
title: Facet Joint Interventions for Pain Management

criteria.criterion: Moderate to severe chronic neck or low back pain, predominantly axial, that causes functional deficit measured on pain or disability scale 6
criteria.source_quote: Moderate to severe chronic neck or low back pain, predominantly axial, that causes functional deficit measured on pain or disability scale 6

criteria.criterion: Pain that has been present for a minimum of 3 months with documented failure to respond to noninvasive conservative care management (as tolerated)
criteria.source_quote: Pain that has been present for a minimum of 3 months with documented failure to respond to noninvasive conservative care management (as tolerated)
criteria.reviewer_note: kept as drafted
criteria.question: Does the note document pain for at least 3 months AND failure of conservative care (for example physical therapy or medications)?

criteria.criterion: Absence of untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except for radiculopathy caused by facet joint synovial cyst)
criteria.source_quote: Absence of untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except for radiculopathy caused by facet joint synovial cyst)
criteria.reviewer_note: kept as drafted
criteria.question: Does the note document untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication?

criteria.criterion: The patient must meet the criteria for the first diagnostic facet joint injection.
criteria.source_quote: For the first diagnostic facet joint injection to be considered medically reasonable and necessary, the patient must meet the criteria outlined under indications for facet joint interventions.
criteria.reviewer_note: applies to repeat/therapeutic/RFA procedures, not a single procedure note in this evaluation

criteria.criterion: The patient must have had 2 medically reasonable and necessary diagnostic facet joint procedures with each one providing a consistent minimum of 80% relief of primary (index) pain.
criteria.source_quote: Therapeutic facet joint injections are considered medically reasonable and necessary for patients who meet ALL the following criteria: - The patient has had 2 medically reasonable and necessary diagnostic facet joint procedures with each one providing a consistent minimum of 80% relief of primary (index) pain (with the duration of relief being consistent with the agent used);
criteria.reviewer_note: applies to repeat/therapeutic/RFA procedures, not a single procedure note in this evaluation

criteria.criterion: Subsequent therapeutic facet joint procedures at the same anatomic site results in at least consistent 50% pain relief for at least 3 months.
criteria.source_quote: Therapeutic facet joint injections are considered medically reasonable and necessary for patients who meet ALL the following criteria: - The patient has had 2 medically reasonable and necessary diagnostic facet joint procedures with each one providing a consistent minimum of 80% relief of primary (index) pain (with the duration of relief being consistent with the agent used); AND - Subsequent therapeutic facet joint procedures at the same anatomic site results in at least consistent 50% pain relief for at least 3 months from the prior therapeutic procedure or at least 50% consistent improvement in the ability to perform previously painful movements and activities of daily living (ADLs) as compared to baseline measurement using the same scale
criteria.reviewer_note: applies to repeat/therapeutic/RFA procedures, not a single procedure note in this evaluation

criteria.criterion: No non-facet pathology per clinical assessment or radiology studies that could explain the source of the patient’s pain.
criteria.source_quote: There is no non-facet pathology per clinical assessment or radiology studies that could explain the source of the patient’s pain, including but not limited to fracture, tumor, infection, or significant deformity.
criteria.reviewer_note: kept as drafted
criteria.question: Does the note document another cause for the pain besides the facet joints (for example fracture, tumor, infection or significant deformity)?

criteria.criterion: No more than 4 diagnostic joint sessions per rolling 12 months.
criteria.source_quote: Frequency limitation : For each covered spinal region no more than 4 diagnostic joint sessions will be considered medically reasonable and necessary per rolling 12 months, in recognition that the pain generator cannot always be identified with the initial and confirmatory diagnostic procedure.
criteria.reviewer_note: needs claims history across visits; cannot be checked from a single procedure note

criteria.criterion: No more than 4 therapeutic facet joint injection sessions per rolling 12 months.

decision_rule.explanation: Policy indications are joined with AND; image guidance, no routine sedation and documented pain scales are also required.

question_note: Each kept criterion is asked as a yes/no question about the note. 'met_if' says which answer satisfies the criterion; 'if_not_mentioned' is used when the note is silent (silence is fine for prohibitions such as sedation, but not for required findings).
